alsoAccept lists other kinds a careful consultant could reasonably choose; a match on any of them counts.
Lerato Dlamini was not asked for consent (she joined late), so T20 and T22 come from a speaker the C11 check lists. Findings may still cite her: C11 is a warning, not a block.

findings.statement: Collections are missed because dispatch runs in a WhatsApp group where messages get buried.
Dispatch is posted in a WhatsApp group, and someone types it into a shared spreadsheet at night.
About 120 collections a day, roughly doubling in November and December, with peak days of up to 260.
Stop missed collections: a re-delivery costs about R1,800, and a retail account was lost over it last December.
A driver can accept a job, mark it collected, photograph the waybill and capture a signature.
The driver's app must work offline for hours (no signal between Colesberg and Beaufort West) and send everything when back in range.
Most drivers have their own Android phones; a few still use basic phones. To be checked.
Do all drivers have smartphones? Pieter to check.
The company would rather not buy phones for every driver.
Trucks have a vendor tracking system, and invoicing runs on Sage.
Pulling truck positions from the tracking system would be useful, but isn't needed at the start.
The MD signs off anything above R200,000; Thandi wants a figure to show her by the end of January.
The Bloemfontein depot's internet goes down during load-shedding (the router isn't on backup power), and then the controller can't see anything.
The consultant proposed that the controller's screen must cope with the depot being offline.
findings.note: Proposed by the consultant, not yet agreed by the client.

findings.statement: May the company use drivers' location data, and how? HR to check with the drivers' union.
Later, clients should get a tracking link, like a courier's.
An Afrikaans version of the app; Pieter says half his drivers would prefer it.
findings.note: Said in answer to 'anything you'd want later', so a future consideration; an NFR is also defensible.

findings.statement: Start with a pilot at the Bloemfontein depot.
The consultant proposed that the app must make sure every collection is assigned and confirmed.
findings.note: The consultant's wording of what the app must do; the client moves on without explicitly agreeing.

findings.statement: Karoo Freight runs forty trucks between Gauteng and the Western Cape, out of two depots, Midrand and Bloemfontein.

notFindings.why: The consent check at the start of the meeting is recorded on the consent form, not in the record.
The consultant's own follow-up (sending a summary) is an action, not a finding about the client.
